![LUNA 3.1.3 demonstration](https://github.com/dnunezx/LUNA/blob/35c7183427913005d58bdb9433ccf6420a9d6167/LUNA-3.1.3-demo.gif?raw=true)

**Starting-disc selection and native in-game disc swapping is fully functional**

>  PSXCore is now the most compatible PS1 emulator available for PS2. Please report any issues you encounter. 

## Changes since LUNA 2.0.0 Stable

### PlayStation games, disc swapping, and in-game return

- Added **PSXCore** integration: discover and launch PS1 VCD games from internal ATA and USB storage alongside PS2 games.
- Added the **L3 platform filter** for Mix, PS2, and PS1 libraries, with saved selection and a brief mode-change notification.
- Added **two-to-four-disc sets** grouped into one library entry. Create, edit, reorder, and remove sets in LUNA, or supply an `.m3u` playlist. Nearby disc-name matches can be offered as suggestions for confirmation.
- Added saved **starting-disc selection** and native **in-game disc swapping**. Hold **L2 + R2 + Select** with one D-pad direction, then release. The pre-launch screen shows the direction-to-disc mapping for the chosen starting disc.
- Added validation of disc identity, missing or duplicate images, changed content, shared volume identity, and memory-card bindings. Changed images can be explicitly revalidated through disc management.
- Added **PS1 in-game return to LUNA**, using the familiar **L1 + L2 + R1 + R2 + Start + Select** combination to open the native menu. Confirm return to load `mc0:/APP_LUNA/luna.elf`.
- Bundled the latest unchanged upstream **PSXCore `360a788`**, including its new LUNA-styled English return menu. **Disc swapping and in-game return are enabled together in this package.**
- Replaced written button names in the disc-swap prompt with controller icons and directional arrows. Added a dark reading panel, brighter and larger text, larger grouped icons, a readable Select button, and clearer disc rows.
- Added per-game **Code Validation** selection, fixed PS1 file launches on exFAT, and added firmware size/hash checks before leaving the library.

### Memory cards and save management

- Added automatic creation of missing **default shared PS1 memory cards**, plus named card pairs and per-game pair selection. Disc sets retain their selected pair across swaps.
- Added a separate **PlayStation card manager** with import, export, paired backups, and recovery of interrupted card operations.
- Connected **PS2 virtual memory-card assignments** to game launches, including the matching OPL runtime and supported APA/PFS mappings.
- Improved card validation, interrupted-operation recovery, settings persistence, and staged-file handling. Existing saves remain on the game drive.

### PS2 launch engines, compatibility, and cheats

- Added **OPL as an alternate PS2 launch engine**, selectable globally or per game; Neutrino remains the default. Bundled OPL backends cover ATA/FAT32/exFAT, APA/HDL, USB, MX4SIO, iLink, MMCE, and UDPFS.
- Added engine-specific compatibility and video controls, clearer default-option summaries, and a dedicated game-core section.
- Added **per-game cheat selection** from `CHT/<TITLE_ID>.cht` through the matching Neutrino runtime. This path uses raw PS2RD codes; cheats are off by default.
- Corrected OPL handoff memory layout and HDD addressing, and fixed launch handling of saved global and per-game startup-logo choices.
- Updated the matching Neutrino runtime, virtual-card handling, and in-game return integration.

### Library views, artwork, and responsiveness

- Redesigned **Scroll** around a horizontal title-logo strip and cover carousel, with depth, a larger selected cover, neighboring-artwork loading, title-text fallback, and glass-themed missing-cover placeholders.
- Scroll logos use `ART/SCROLL/<TITLE_ID>_LGO.png`. Removed the old per-title wallpaper and game-information panel from Scroll.
- Added **PS1 jewel-case or tall-case styling** in List and 3D, plus configurable Separate or Overlap cover/disc layout in List. View appearance controls now sit together under Views.
- Added **3D page transitions**, softer case thumbnails, and safer artwork uploads while drawing.
- Improved **Collections** entry with seven prepared covers, cached-artwork reuse, and fewer loading interruptions.
- Improved **Orbit** cover reuse and crossfades, reducing flashing placeholders during browsing.
- Optimized artwork caching, thumbnail reuse, visible List rows, game lookup, Favorites updates, and view switching for larger libraries.
- Restored and preserved **stable 2.0 animation and navigation timing** in Collections and Orbit while retaining artwork optimizations.

### Backgrounds, languages, and menus

- Added animated backgrounds including **Neo, Aurora, Ronin, Gridrunner, Torch, and Tempest**, with a nighttime Gridrunner scene.
- Added saved **English, Spanish, and Brazilian Portuguese** selection, translated UI text, and UTF-8 support in both fonts.
- Added configurable **Ambient Orbs formations**, including skull and atom shapes, with saved enabled-shape choices.
- Polished the main menu and Options layout, blue selection accents, focus highlights, glass contrast, default-value summaries, and save feedback.
- Improved quick-menu readability and closing behavior, added R1 dismissal, and removed duplicate icon shadows.
- Fixed menu-title alignment, font fading, and overlapping per-game video-mode text.

### File Explorer and storage

- Expanded **File Explorer** with storage and memory-card browsing, folder navigation, paging, contextual actions, and clearer button prompts.
- Added a persistent **copy tray**, multi-item marking, copy/move workflows, transfer progress, and **Skip / Keep Both / Replace** choices for name conflicts.
- Added folder creation, rename, deletion, file/folder details, filtering, and sorting by name, size, or date. Moves verify copied data before removing their source.
- Added read-only **text/configuration previews** and direct launching of compatible PS2 homebrew ELF files after confirmation.
- Improved storage rescans, including empty-library recovery and preserving the display during refreshes.

### Reliability and packaging

- Fixed hardware-freeze causes involving runtime locks, artwork upload limits, and worker-stack reuse during shutdown.
- Hardened ISO scanning and title-cache validation. Scan and transfer failures preserve previous library state and move sources.
- Improved recovery of staged Favorites saves, configuration writes, graphics-allocation failures, texture lifetimes, and repeated cleanup.
- Bundled matching hardware builds of LUNA, PSXCore, Neutrino, and OPL, with license notices and SHA-256 checksums. Optional music remains a separate add-on.

## Installation

Download **`LUNA-v3.1.3-FMCB-mc0.zip`**, extract it, and copy the complete **`APP_LUNA`** folder to **`mc0:/APP_LUNA`**. 

For PS1 games, place VCD images and optional `.m3u` playlists under **`/VCD/`** on a HDD or USB drive. Supply your own matching **`/POPS/POPS.ELF`** and **`/POPS/IOPRP252.IMG`**. Firmware, games, and saves are not included,

## Verification

The versioned hardware launcher, unchanged PSXCore runtime, Neutrino runtime, and OPL backends built successfully. PSXCore launch-layout validation, package file checks, ZIP contents, and SHA-256 checksums passed.

[Full source changes since LUNA 2.0.0 Stable](https://github.com/dnunezx/LUNA/compare/v2.0.0...v3.1.3)

First published build of the SHELF UI for Open PS2 Loader.

## Which file do I want?

| Asset | For |
|---|---|
| `OPNPS2LD-MMCE.ELF` | **Most people.** Built from the MMCE fork; supports memory-card SD devices (SD2PSX, MemCard PRO2) |
| `OPNPS2LD-mainline.ELF` | Mainline OPL only. **Has no MMCE support at all** — flashing this on an MMCE setup makes the memory-card SD disappear |

Put the file wherever your chip already boots OPL from — usually
`mc0:/OPL/OPNPS2LD.ELF`, or `mmce0:/APPS/OPNPS2LD.ELF` on an SD2PSX under FMCB.
See [docs/INSTALL.md](../blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) and
[docs/BOOTING.md](../blob/main/docs/BOOTING.md).

Some tools (`tools/stage-device.sh`, `tools/sync-card.sh`) expect the MMCE build
at `patches/build/OPNPS2LD-MMCE.ELF`; download it there if you use them.

## What's in it

- **SHELF** — a sidebar shell with Home, Library, Apps and Settings pages, drawn
  over OPL rather than configured through it. Open it with **L3** from anywhere.
- **Grid themes** — `ItemsList` lays out a real grid, `GameImage` can address a
  slot other than the highlighted one, with two-axis navigation.
- **Sort modes, recently-played, `MenuTabs`, play stats, texture-safety fixes.**
- Builds with `IGS=1`, so **D-pad Up** takes an in-game screenshot where GSM is
  enabled for that title.

## Status, honestly

SHELF has been run on real hardware and phase 4 was verified at 480p. Phase 8
(game grouping) is not started. The standalone theme patches `01`–`03` compile
clean with zero warnings and their effect is confirmed by diffing section sizes
against an unpatched build, but they have not been booted in isolation.

**Test on a setup you can recover.** On an FMCB setup the no-button boot path is
your fallback: it runs the ELF baked inside the card image, which nothing here
touches. If a build hangs, power-cycle without holding L1.

## Verifying

These are LZMA-packed, so `strings` on them returns compressed noise and finds
none of the feature strings — that is expected and is not evidence of a bad
build. Verify against `opl.elf` in a build tree instead.

| Asset | Size | MD5 |

| `OPNPS2LD-MMCE.ELF` | 1,389,876 | `07f7fb7b2c0e56202054ca3bb02aa88a` |
| `OPNPS2LD-mainline.ELF` | 1,363,860 | `6962fc05af24a31551864a2235bcedfc` |

Source for these binaries is this repository: the patches in `patches/`, and the

## PS2 Manager 2.1.0

### 🌍 Language
* **Language picker** in Settings → Appearance: System, Italiano or English.
* PS2 Manager asks to relaunch to apply it (**Relaunch Now** / **Later**) and reopens once it has really quit.

### 📥 Install / Update
```bash
brew install --cask gionnio/tap/ps2-manager
brew upgrade --cask ps2-manager
```

PS2 Manager is not signed with an Apple Developer ID. If macOS blocks the first launch, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway** (right-click → Open no longer works on macOS 15 or later).

A small one: covers show up right away again.

**Website, screenshots, setup guide:** https://danielnuld.github.io/ps2-launcher/

## Fixed

- **Covers took a long time to appear** with the network cable in. In v1.0.1 the covers on screen waited for the
  launcher's network work at boot (downloading missing covers, asking about achievements), so they could show up
  only when the achievements chip did. The thread that loads them now goes first.

Everything from [v1.0.1](https://github.com/danielnuld/ps2-launcher/releases/tag/v1.0.1) is in here too: USB games
booting on a real PS2, up to 1024 games, DNS with DHCP, MemCard PRO 2 game IDs.

## Updating

Copy `launcher.elf` from the zip over the one on your USB drive (from v1.0, copy `neutrino/` too). Your `orbit/`
folder, covers and virtual memory cards stay as they are.

## Known issues

- The in-game menu doesn't react to a DualSense on an 8BitDo adapter; a wired controller works (#11).
- "Native" video mode can give a black screen on some setups: keep the default 480p.
- Loading over udpfs needs a wired network on both ends; Neutrino's UDP transport does not recover from WiFi
  packet loss.

## The console launcher

`ophtml.elf` turns any ps2ui theme into a game launcher: it loads USB, exFAT

### Added

- **The OPHTML console: any ps2ui theme, driven as a game launcher
  (`console/`).** Until now a baked UI could draw a game list and do
  nothing with it: the runtime is display-only by design, and device
  I/O and launching were the app's to write, so nobody's UI could list
  or start a game. `ophtml.elf` loads USB, exFAT HDD, MX4SIO and MMCE

  (title IDs from the name or the disc's `SYSTEM.CNF`), fills whatever
  theme it finds — `theme.uib` beside the ELF, then `OPHTML/theme.uib`
  on a drive, then the built-in `examples/console` — and hands the
  selected game to Neutrino with `-qb` through elf-loader's no-reset
  entry point, so Neutrino reads it through the drivers the console
  loaded. A theme opts in by using names (`game-{i}` rows,
  `game-{i}-title`, `sel-title`, `status` and the rest in
  `console/README.md`), every one optional; nothing in C is the
  author's to write. Proven so far: `console/tests` on the host (file
  names, ISO9660, `SYSTEM.CNF`, the directory scan, Neutrino's command
  line), and `hw.yml` booting a MOCK build in Play! and diffing its
  filled list against the previewer drawing the same games. Not yet:
  no drive has been mounted and no game started on a console. Bench
  cases C1–C8 in `console/README.md` are that evidence, and each is
  open.

- **A console theme can be checked, previewed and navigated before it
  reaches a console.** `ps2ui check` holds any blob with numbered
  `game-N` rows or slots to the console's contract: an error for a row the console would
  leave on its placeholder (a gap in `game-N`, rows on a screen it never
  opens, a slot for a row that doesn't exist), a warning for a name it
  never fills (`game-0-titel`, with "did you mean 'title'?"), a slot too
  short for what it writes, or rows with no title; `ps2ui-check
  --console` forces it on a blob with none. `sel-*` and `status` alone
  do not opt a blob in, because other UIs use them for their own panels
  (channel-6 has five sel-* slots); a blob with no numbered row gets
  none of these results, so every other blob's count is unchanged. `ps2ui serve --console` fills a theme with the mock games
  and walks its list the way the console does. And `hw.yml` now presses
  buttons at the console in Play! — Down three times, R1, L1 — and
  diffs each frame against the previewer replaying the same keys
  (worst tile 14.4-15.1 correct, 62-72 for a selection or window one
  step off). That build runs on the ROM's pad modules, because Play!
  gives the SDK's `sio2man`+`freepad` no input after an IOP reset
  (measured against the ROM pair, which it does answer); so it proves
  the console's navigation, and `freepad` stays bench case C8. The
  contract, the mock list and the list window now live in
  `ps2ui_bake/console.py`, which the check, the server and CI's
  reference frames all read.
- **Hard caps on what an untrusted theme may ask the compilers for.** A
  theme is a file somebody else wrote, and the compilers accepted
  whatever it asked for. Four caps now, each measured before it was
  chosen: canvas dimensions at 2048, elements at 10000, nesting at 64,
  and a source image at 32 megapixels. Every one is overridable in
  `ps2ui.json` beside `vramBudget` -- `{"limits": {"nodes": 40000}}` --
  because a cap with no escape gets edited out of the source by the
  first person it blocks.

  The numbers come from the shipped corpus rather than from taste.
  Across all 17 screens in `examples/` and `fixtures/`, counted with the
  compiler's own walk after `data-repeat` expands, the largest is 93
  elements at depth 5, every supported mode is 640x448 or 640x512, and
  the largest source image is 1984x1408. The headroom is each cap's
  own: about 108x for elements, about 13x for depth, and for the canvas
  none of that kind at all, because 2048 is the widest framebuffer the
  hardware scans out rather than a multiple of anything the corpus
  says. *"An order of magnitude above the biggest real thing"* stood
  here until it was read back against the three.

  They fail rather than warn, which is the opposite of what
  `check-doc-impact.py` argues for itself and right for the same reason:
  a warning is correct where the work might be fine, and a PlayStation 2
  cannot display a 30000px canvas under any circumstances.

  The escape hatch broke two verbs before it worked. `ps2ui check` was
  sent a `--limit` it does not take, and `ps2ui dev` was sent one it
  did not take either -- the project-file page had listed `limits` as
  reaching dev the whole time -- so a project declaring any cap got
  `unrecognized arguments` from the first and a bare usage line from
  the second, while `ps2ui build` on the same file was fine. Both are
  fixed, and the fence is a test that reads the spawned tool's own
  parser rather than a list maintained beside it. And the flag reached

  two CLI pages and the diagnostics catalogue now carry `--limit`, the

  sabotage after that found one more: each cap has a test that its
  check fires, and the image cap was the one whose *number* nothing
  read, so raising it to ten billion left the whole suite green. It is
  held to the corpus, to the default an ordinary bake gets, and to the
  figure the project-file page prints. `ps2ui-bake --limit
  nodes=5` says so too now: a real cap, correctly spelled, handed to
  the tool that does not enforce it, answered until now by
  *"takes imagePixels=N with N a positive integer"* -- a complaint
  about the 5.

- **The console launcher can be downloaded, and the docs site says how
  to run it.** Until now `ophtml.elf` existed only as a CI artifact,
  which needs a GitHub login and expires after fourteen days, or as a
  Docker build of this repository. `console-release.yml` now runs when
  a version is tagged: it bakes the built-in theme, builds `ophtml.elf`
  and `ophtml-mock.elf` from the tag, and attaches both with
  `SHA256SUMS` to that tag's GitHub Release. A tag with no release gets

  installing Neutrino, putting your own `theme.uib` beside the ELF,
  the names the launcher fills, the controls, and what each status
  line and start-up colour means. It opens by saying the launcher has
  booted only in an emulator, and it points at the bench cases that
  are still open.

- **A released CHANGELOG section is held to its tag.** A merge in #166
  put four entries into the released `## 0.8.0` section with no conflict
  marker, and every `tools/check-*.py` passed on that state (F53).
  `check-versions.py` rule 23 now compares each release tag's section,
  heading and body, with `git show <tag>:CHANGELOG.md`, and fails on a
  difference. The one legitimate difference, v0.3.0's "Tagged and
  published" paragraph written after its tag, is recorded with its
  reason and pinned by hash, so it excuses that text and nothing else.
  The rule runs on pull requests too, which is where that merge was.

- **The `.uib` loader is fuzzed (S2).** `runtime/tests/fuzz_load.c`
  runs libFuzzer over `ps2ui_arena_size`, `ps2ui_load` and everything a
  program does with a blob that loaded, under ASan and UBSan, seeded
  from every blob the repository builds, with each mutation's CRC
  rewritten the way a hostile file would carry one. `ci.yml` gives it
  60 seconds on every change, and `fuzz.yml` gives it half an hour
  nightly, keeping its corpus between nights. `make -C runtime fuzz`
  runs it locally. The Python half, `test_fuzz_uib.py`, mutates the
  example blobs and requires `read_uib` to raise only ValueError and
  `ps2ui check` never to raise. Both found real faults, listed under
  Fixed.

### Changed

- **`registry.yml` stops carrying 0.8.0's fribidi remedy, now that 0.9.0
  is what a stranger installs.** It kept the macOS and Windows remedy
  steps, and the `-plain` jobs' assertion that fontgen refuses, while the
  published release still needed Raqm, switching on whether the wheel
  carried `_raqm_remedy`. 0.9.0 published, and run 35817721457 passed
  every arm against it: the tutorial on all four with the remedies
  skipped, and the committed tables from a plain install on macOS arm64,
  macOS x86_64 and Windows. The remedies, the switch and the refusal
  assertions are deleted. What replaces the switch is a guard: the
  first run after the publish, 35817387412, was served 0.8.0 on both
  Macs by an index that had not caught up, and the old refusal passed
  there, measuring nothing. The `-plain` jobs now fail by name when pip
  hands them a release from before F47, rather than later in fontgen
  with a message that blames the machine.

### Fixed

- **A crafted `.uib` could crash the console before anything drew.**
  Nothing checked where a table sat, only that it fit, and every table
  is read in place through a struct pointer. On the EE a misaligned
  32-bit load is an address error. The fuzzer's first run found
  `ps2ui_arena_size`, the first call a program makes on a blob, reading
  the slot table at an odd address. The console launcher makes that
  call on any `theme.uib` it finds on a drive. `ps2ui_load` now refuses
  a blob address, a table, or a font's glyph or kern table that is not
  4-byte aligned, with `PS2UI_ERR_ALIGN`, and `ps2ui_arena_size`
  returns 0 for one. Every blob the baker writes passes: its header is
  84 bytes, every entry a multiple of 4, and glyph and kern tables are
  16-aligned.

- **`ps2ui check` printed a Python traceback for a malformed blob.**
  `read_uib` promises ValueError on a bad file, and `ps2ui check`
  catches that and prints the message. A table running past the end,
  an unknown texture format or a glyph table outside the blob raised
  `struct.error` or `KeyError` instead. A blob that read cleanly but
  referenced past a table got `IndexError` from whichever later check
  subscripted it. The reader now checks every table's extent and
  alignment as the runtime does and refuses unknown formats. When a
  reference or a screen range is bad, the checks that walk them are
  skipped and the report says so; any other error stops nothing.

- **A raised VRAM budget bought room for a framebuffer, which no budget
  can.** `--vram-budget` exists to let a project declare the texture
  space it really has. The refusal for a canvas too large to scan out
  lived inside the advice printed only when no budget was given, so
  passing one silenced the sentence and the failure together: a
  30000x30000 canvas baked to a 17760-byte blob with exit 0, past a
  message whose own last line reads "a narrower canvas is the only fix".
  The budget charges textures and a framebuffer is not a texture, so the
  check is now separate from the one a flag can reach.

- **A 439 KiB image could cost 432 MB and eleven seconds, or end the
  bake in a traceback.** An image is pre-scaled to its laid-out size, so
  the baked bytes were already bounded: 40 distinct 1024x1024 sources
  bake to 40 KiB. Nothing bounded the decode. A 12000x12000 PNG baked
  clean in 11.0 seconds to produce 4 KiB of texture, and one step larger
  Pillow's own `DecompressionBombError` reached the terminal raw. The
  size is read from the header now, before any decode, so the same file
  fails in 0.08 seconds with one error line.

- **Nesting deep enough reported `Maximum call stack size
  exceeded`.** That is V8's stack rather than a decision, so the real
  limit moved with the machine and the message named neither the
  element nor a number. How far it moves, bisected on one checkout:
  1842 on node v22.22.2's default stack, 889 under `--stack-size=500`,
  7781 under `--stack-size=4000`. The first version of this entry said
  *"deeper than about 1500"*, which was the midpoint of the
  1000-compiled / 2000-died bracket written as though it were a
  reading; review of #166 asked for the reading. The refusal is the compiler's now, at 64, and
  names the line the deepest element sits on. The check is iterative,
  because a recursive walk to find the depth that breaks a recursive
  walk overflows before it can report anything.

## OPL com Bluetooth (DS4 clone / DualSense) via dongle USB

Fork do Open PS2 Loader com suporte a controles sem fio Bluetooth no PADEMU, usando um dongle Bluetooth USB no PS2.

### Novidades
- Suporte a **DualShock 4 original e clones ("Wireless Controller")** e **DualSense** pelo PADEMU, no menu e dentro do jogo.
- **Dongles Realtek RTL8761B(U)**: o firmware é carregado automaticamente ao iniciar (menu e jogo).
- **Pareamento sem fio** pela tela PADEMU > Bluetooth Pads (busca, lista de dispositivos, chaves guardadas na configuração).
- **Vibração no jogo** funcionando em DS4/clones (relatório de saída com CRC32, handshake do relatório 0x05, buffers L2CAP sem corrida).
- Motor grande da vibração com faixa ampliada (96–255), porque os clones quase não respondem a valores baixos.
- Menu minimalista
- MULTITAP EMU + Misto com Controle Real

### Correção: Kingdom Hearts II (SLPM-66675) com PADEMU + SMB
Com o PADEMU ligado e a ISO no SMB, o KH2 não iniciava o som: o jogo pede 233.432 bytes **contínuos** da RAM da IOP para o buffer de efeitos sonoros e a alocação falhava (`SE(fffffffc)`). O PADEMU, o USBD e a pilha de rede deixavam o total livre e o maior bloco contínuo abaixo disso. O que mudou:
- **Pilha de rede in-game (SMSTCPIP) sem remontagem/fragmentação IP.** Os buffers estáticos de remontagem (5,8 KB) e fragmentação (1,5 KB) ficavam residentes sem serem usados (TCP sobre MTU 1500 não fragmenta).
- **Pool do USBD menor** para o PADEMU (endpoints 10, TDs 12, isoTDs 2, requisições 8), já que só um dongle Bluetooth é usado.
- **Builds de debug** passam a usar o mesmo lwIP enxuto do release (com UDP para o log), para o log refletir a memória real. Antes eles usavam o lwIP completo, e por isso os ajustes de memória nunca apareciam nos testes.
- Mantidos `CDVDMAN_FS_SECTORS = 8` e a janela TCP de 10240 / 8 buffers: reduzi esses valores numa tentativa e o SMB caiu de ~9 ms para ~318 ms por leitura de 16 KB (~50 KB/s), e leituras de 3 setores travavam o FMV.
- Resultado medido no build de debug: o KH2 passa a alocar o buffer de efeitos (`SE(038fd8/038fd8:100%)`) com ~30 KB de sobra, e o SMB volta a ~8 ms por leitura.

### Como usar
1. Copie `OPL-DualSense-BT-*.ELF` para o PS2 e execute.
2. Espete o dongle Bluetooth numa porta USB do PS2.
3. Em **Configurações > PADEMU**, escolha o modo **DS3/DS4/DS5 BT** e use **Bluetooth Pads > Search** com o controle em modo de pareamento (PS + Share).
4. Ative o PADEMU no jogo e jogue.

### Limitações conhecidas
- **Este é um release candidato:** a correção do KH2 foi validada num build de debug. Houve uma trava aos ~22 s do primeiro FMV nesse build de debug, ainda sob investigação (suspeita: log por UDP em alta taxa); o build de release ainda não foi testado nesse ponto.
- O KH2 em SMB com PADEMU tem pouca folga de memória. Rodar a ISO por USB ou HDD libera a pilha de rede inteira da IOP.
- A cor do LED de alguns clones ainda não muda (em investigação).
- Sem teste em todos os modelos de dongle: relate o VID/PID do seu em uma issue.

### Créditos
Baseado no Open PS2 Loader e no PADEMU. Dongle Realtek: firmware do projeto linux-firmware.

# Open PS2 Loader Extended APA - Hardware-Tested Release 1

This is the first public hardware-tested release of **Open PS2 Loader Extended APA**.

It is intended for PlayStation 2 internal HDDs larger than 2 TiB that have been prepared using the matching **Extended APA / banked APA** layout.

## Real-hardware validation

Validated on a real PlayStation 2 with a 4 TB HDD:

- FHDB / FreeHDBoot boot works.
- Bank 0 HDL games are detected and launch.
- Bank 1 HDL games are detected and launch.
- OPL artwork and configuration remain in Bank 0 and work for Bank 1 games.
- Bank 0 remains the conventional APA/PFS system and application area.

## Layout

- **Bank 0:** conventional bootable APA/PFS + FHDB + OPL + applications/art/config + optional HDL games.
- **Bank 1+:** games-only APA banks.

Each full bank covers `0x100000000` 512-byte sectors (2 TiB). Upper-bank APA addresses remain bank-relative; OPL translates them to physical LBAs using the bank base.

```text
physical_lba = (bank_index * 0x100000000) + relative_lba
```

See `EXTENDED_APA.md` for the complete technical description and Mermaid diagram.

## Exact tested build

- OPL base version: `v1.2.0-Beta-2273`
- Extended APA source commit: `b2e39f0d6b569cf79a3235dc47050016d102cd31`
- Release ELF SHA-256: `aa7d6765f88fec8d059ebb4fafc76e75e5cd8f8820e083fec0f45640ed32a244`

The attached ELF is the exact CI-produced binary used for the successful hardware test. It is intentionally pinned so PS2 HDD Manager can download and verify a known-good Extended APA loader when provisioning drives larger than 2 TiB.

## Important

This remains experimental. It is not required for ordinary <=2 TiB APA HDDs. Use official Open PS2 Loader for normal configurations unless Extended APA support is specifically required.

A >2 TiB Extended APA disk must be prepared by a compatible formatter/writer. An official OPL build will not enumerate the upper APA banks.

### PS2 Servers Edge — routers, NAS, Raspberry Pi

The `PS2ServersEdge-*` files are the native headless edition, with an optional
web dashboard and no Python runtime, for
devices where the launcher does not fit — routers, NAS units, Raspberry Pi and
other embedded Linux. Windows and macOS builds exist for people who want one
native binary and no Python runtime.

Each file is named for the device family it serves, for example
`armv5-pogoplug-sheevaplug-dockstar`, `edgerouter-octeon-mips64`, or
`router-mips-little-endian-mt7621`. Run `uname -m` on the device and match it in
[EDGE-WHICH-BUILD.md](https://github.com/NathanNeurotic/PS2-Servers/blob/main/docs/EDGE-WHICH-BUILD.md);
every archive also contains a `WHICH-DEVICE.txt` confirming what it is for.
An incompatible build usually refuses to start; verify the OS and architecture
before installing it.

Edge serves **three** protocols, one subcommand each, and can run more than one
at a time:

```sh
ps2servers-edge udpfs --root /mnt/games      # folder as a network file share
ps2servers-edge udpbd --image /mnt/ps2.img   # disk image as a network drive
ps2servers-edge smb   --share games=/mnt/games   # SMBv1, for OPL and POPSTARTER

# folder AND a disk image from one server, over UDPFS block access
ps2servers-edge udpfs --root /mnt/games --block-device /mnt/ps2.img
```

`smb` is what OPL's own network game list and POPSTARTER use. It listens on
**TCP port `1111`** rather than 445, because ports below 1024 need root and Edge
runs unprivileged — set OPL's "SMB Port" to match.

There is also a fourth subcommand, `webui`, which serves a small web dashboard
for configuring and restarting the others from a phone or a browser. **It binds
`127.0.0.1` and refuses to start on any other address without a password**
(`--auth-pass`, or `--insecure` to have one generated and logged), because it
rewrites configuration and restarts services — reaching it is equivalent to
shell access on the device. It speaks plain HTTP, so the password stops casual
access on the LAN, not someone capturing traffic.

Edge supports **CSO and ZSO but not CHD** (CHD needs a native library that would
break static linking — use the Desktop app for CHD). It **allows the console to
write by default**; saves require a client that supports that write path.
Pass `--read-only` to prevent writes. `--metrics`
logs periodic transfer statistics, which is the way to tell a slow transfer from
a stalled one on a machine with no screen. `--compression-cache-size` tunes how
many decompressed blocks are held per image, which matters most on the slowest
devices.

For OpenWrt, build the source package for your exact target rather than using
these generic binaries — see
[OPENWRT.md](https://github.com/NathanNeurotic/PS2-Servers/blob/main/docs/OPENWRT.md).
The OpenWrt package starts read-only; set `option read_only '0'` in
`/etc/config/ps2servers-edge` to let the console save. The UCI configuration exposes the serving options, including `block_device`;
CLI-only flags such as `--quiet` are not UCI options. Each subcommand is its own procd
instance, so a board can serve UDPFS and SMB at once. There are systemd units
for the same thing on ordinary Linux, where `systemctl restart
ps2servers-edge@smb` does restart just that one.

On OpenWrt the dashboard's **Save and Restart need root** — `uci commit` rewrites
a file in `/etc/config` and restarting goes through `/etc/init.d` — so they are
off by default and report a permission error. Status, configuration and file
browsing all work regardless. Set `option run_as_root '1'` to enable them, which
runs the dashboard as root; that is a real trade, which is why it is a choice.

> **Edge gameplay and writes have not been verified on a physical PlayStation 2 or an emulator.** Its
> wire behaviour is checked in CI against the hardware-validated Python servers,
> including a byte-for-byte comparison for UDPBD, which is the strongest evidence
> available without a console — and not the same thing as one. Treat the write
> paths as unproven.

## Security transparency

PS2 Servers is an open-source PS2 homebrew utility for user-controlled local
server setup. It runs local LAN servers for Open PS2 Loader:

- **SMBv1** — guest file sharing. Desktop defaults to TCP `1025`; Core/standalone
  and Edge default to TCP port `1111`. Match the running server’s printed port.
- **SMB2/SMB3** — a separate, newer server for clients that speak them,
  off by default and with NTLMv2 authentication when credentials are set.
- **UDPFS** — UDP file serving, normally UDP port `0xF5F6` (62966).
- **UDPBD** — UDP block-device serving, normally UDP port `0xBDBD` (48573).
- **HTTP game serving** — experimental, read-only, normally TCP `1100`;
  distinct from Edge’s management dashboard. Set the client port explicitly.

For UDPFS, Auto negotiates Standard/Modulo per peer. If games list but fail to
launch on a multi-interface PC, use the UDPFS card’s **Bind address (PC)** /
**Use LAN IP**, then stop/start UDPFS. The top LAN IP selector alone supplies
setup hints. See [UDPFS setup](https://github.com/NathanNeurotic/PS2-Servers/blob/main/README.md#udpfs-games-list-but-fail-to-launch).

The PS2 Servers Edge build additionally offers an optional HTTP management
dashboard on TCP `8082` (`ps2servers-edge webui`). It is **off by default**,
binds loopback when started, and refuses any other bind address without a
password. No listener is opened unless you start it.

Every server here is started by the user and listens on the local network only.
Nothing phones home, and nothing opens a port at install time.

Windows behavior:

Direct-link setup also requires elevation to configure/restore its dedicated
interface and DHCP helper. Disable it before removing the app. The launcher
stores per-user settings (including configured credentials); manually installed
services and containers require separate cleanup.


- The Windows SMB server uses PS2 Servers' built-in SMB/CIFS implementation and does not enable Windows SMB1.
- The app does not enable or disable Windows optional features.

**Using the config**

You only need `ember-launcher.cfg` if the launcher is NOT in the same folder as `ember.elf`. If it is, the file is ignored.

1. Keep `ember-launcher.cfg` in the same folder as the launcher.
2. Open it in a text editor and remove the `#` from the line for your device. Change the folder name if yours isn't `EMBER`.
3. Start the launcher. Your games are listed from that folder's `games/` as usual.

Common lines:

    ember=mmce?:/EMBER/                  MMCE (SD2PSX, MemCard PRO2)
    ember=mass:/EMBER/                   USB
    ember=mx4sio:/EMBER/                 MX4SIO
    ember=ata:/EMBER/                    Internal HDD, exFAT
    ember=hdd0:<partition>:pfs:/EMBER/   Internal HDD, APA/PFS

Point it at the folder that holds `ember.elf`, not at `ember.elf` itself or a game. If you leave every line commented out, the launcher searches MMCE, USB, exFAT HDD, MX4SIO and memory cards for `EMBER/ember.elf` on its own. APA/PFS hard disks and network shares always need their line.

# POPSLoader 1.3.1

This maintenance release includes the controller-free boot fix and larger disc artwork, with the existing Ember Beta-2 option and complete installation kit.

## Changes

- **Boot without a controller in port 1 (#603):** disconnected/error pads stop initialization immediately; transient readiness waits are bounded to one second. The port remains open for a controller connected later. The error-screen button poll also returns without waiting on unavailable input.
- **Readable disc artwork (#568):** matching `<gamefilename>_ICO.png` art now draws at approximately 45% of the case height (112-pixel cap), inside the preview panel and clear of game titles. Loading stays asynchronous.
- Includes the current black-fade launch/video transitions, Ember integration and complete installable ZIP / eight-file flat PSU package from the development channel.
- **Issues #603 and #568 remain open for their reporters to verify and close.**

## Downloads

- `PS1_POPSLOADER.zip`: device-root installation kit with `APPS/PS1_POPSLOADER/`, pinned `POPS/` and `EMBER/` trees, and the flat PSU.
- `PS1_POPSLOADER.psu`: the same eight app files directly under the `PS1_POPSLOADER` save header; POPS and EMBER support folders are installed separately from the ZIP.
- `POPSLOADER.ELF`: standalone executable.
- `BUILD-MANIFEST.txt` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`: exact source/CI provenance and asset checksums.

## Validation and limitations

Automated gates cover the real controller source, embedded Lua runtime, NTSC/PAL disc layout, PNG decoding, UDPFS configuration/integration and package contents. The official assets come from the exact passing master CI run.

**Physical-console verification of #603 and #568 is pending.** Ember game launch, controller behavior after handoff, writable VMC saves and UDPFS/storage compatibility still require recorded PS2 tests. Ember and USB + UDPFS remain experimental options within this official launcher release. i.Link for Ember remains deferred.

Ember is Gageformer's existing, unmodified **Beta-2**, not a new emulator release. Its upstream license ships with the kit. Supply your own BIOS, games and proprietary Sony POPS components as needed; none are provided. `ExampleGame.bin` is an empty placement example.

      HDUI-BG.CFG      ordem do fundo


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 4. INSTALACAO, PASSO A PASSO
----------------------------------------------------------------------

 PASSO 1 - A SUITE
   1. Ligue o HD (ou pendrive) no PC.
   2. Descompacte o Vxx_retrovolt_full.zip na RAIZ dele.
      Fica G:\RETROVOLT\... (G: = a letra do seu HD/pendrive).
   3. Ja tem uma pasta RETROVOLT? Descompacte POR CIMA. O pacote so
      troca os programas; seus jogos, capas, saves e memory cards
      virtuais continuam la.

 PASSO 2 - O NEUTRINO (jogos de PS2)
   1. Baixe o pacote mais novo do Neutrino (projeto oficial no GitHub).
   2. Copie para G:\RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\ os TRES itens juntos:
        neutrino.elf   +   pasta config\   +   pasta modules\
   3. Nunca misture versoes (neutrino.elf de uma, config/modules de
      outra): da tela preta. Ao atualizar, troque os tres de uma vez.
   4. Onde o loader procura o Neutrino, nesta ordem:
        1) pendrive: RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\neutrino.elf
        2) pendrive, na raiz: neutrino.elf
        3) HD: RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\neutrino.elf
        4) memory card: mc0:RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\neutrino.elf
      Use UMA copia so. Com duas, vale a primeira da lista (e as
      configuracoes da outra sao ignoradas).

 PASSO 3 - O EMBER (jogos de PS1)
   1. Crie a pasta EMBER na RAIZ do HD ou do pendrive (fora do RETROVOLT).
   2. Coloque nela o ember.elf (Beta 2 ou mais novo) e a bios.bin do
      seu proprio console.
   3. Dentro dela, crie a pasta games\ e uma pasta para cada jogo, com o
      .cue e o .bin dentro. Jogo de varios discos: todos os .cue/.bin na
      mesma pasta.
   4. O PS1 so funciona pelo HD ou pelo pendrive (ainda nao pelo MX4SIO
      nem pelo MMCE).

 PASSO 4 - OS JOGOS DE PS2
   1. Copie as ISOs para o HD/pendrive, em qualquer pasta ate 4 niveis
      abaixo da raiz (ex.: DVD\, CD\, JOGOS\).
   2. Nao coloque ISOs dentro de RETROVOLT, EMBER ou APPS: essas pastas
      nao sao lidas na busca.
   3. Pendrive em FAT32: ISO de 4 GB ou mais nao cabe. Use exFAT.

 PASSO 5 - OS JOGOS DO RETRO ARCADE
   CPS1 / CPS2 / MVS:
     - ROMs (.zip do MAME) em EXTRAS\CPS1\ROMS, CPS2\ROMS e MVS\ROMS.
     - O rominfo e o zipname de cada sistema ficam na pasta do sistema
       (EXTRAS\CPS1\rominfo.cps1, zipname.cps1 ...). Sem eles a aba nao
       aparece.
     - CPS2: cada jogo precisa do CACHE, gerado no PC a partir do .zip
       (romcnv_cps2.exe / gerar_caches.bat), em EXTRAS\CPS2\CACHE.
     - MVS: a BIOS neogeo.zip vai em EXTRAS\MVS\ROMS. Jogos grandes
       tambem usam cache em EXTRAS\MVS\CACHE.
     - CPS2 e Neo-Geo pesados: use o HD interno (exFAT). No pendrive e
       no MX4SIO podem engasgar.
   PC ENGINE:
     - HuCard (.pce) ou ISO (.cue + .bin) em EXTRAS\PCE\ROMS, ou o CD
       original no leitor.
   NEO GEO CD:
     - Coloque o CD (original ou gravado) no leitor do PS2. A BIOS ja
       vem dentro do nucleo. A pasta EXTRAS\NEOGEO-CD precisa existir.

 PASSO 6 - O PROGRAMA DE WINDOWS (opcional)
   Abra o RetroVoltSuite.exe (nao precisa instalar).
   - Idioma: na 1a vez ele pergunta "Portugues (PT-BR) / English (ENG)".
     Trocar depois: caixa de idioma no canto de cima, a direita (o
     programa reabre no idioma novo). Fica gravado no RetroVoltSuite.ini.
   - Parou o mouse em cima de um botao ou opcao: aparece um balao
     explicando o que ele faz.
   - Aba "Capas e MCV":
       1. "Escolher unidade dos jogos...": escolha a unidade (HD/pendrive)
          onde estao os jogos. O programa varre TUDO sozinho (raiz, CD,
          DVD, EMBER\games...). Nessa unidade ele tambem cria a estrutura
          RETROVOLT que faltar e, se as pastas da suite estiverem em
          minusculo (retrovolt, fastloader, capas...), passa para
          MAIUSCULO. Nunca cria CD nem DVD.
       2. Capa, logo e disco que voce copiou a mao para
          RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\CAPAS\PS2 (ou PS1) com o nome do jogo
          (JOGO.PNG, JOGO_LOGO.PNG, JOGO_ICO.PNG) contam como "Ja existe no
          dispositivo" na proxima leitura - o jogo deixa de ficar vermelho.
       3. "Escolher unidade de destino...": o HD/pendrive do PS2. O destino
          comeca SEMPRE vazio: voce decide. O programa cria o que faltar
          em RETROVOLT (e so em RETROVOLT; nunca no disco do Windows).
       4. "Baixar e gerar capas": baixa capa, logo e disco de cada jogo.
          O que ja existe so e trocado com "Sobrescrever capas que ja
          existem" ligado.
       5. Coluna MCV + "Criar MCV dos jogos marcados": cria memory cards
          virtuais de 8 MB, ja formatados.
   - Aba "Retroarcade": capas dos jogos de CPS1, CPS2, MVS e PC Engine.
   - Aba "Rede": servidor para jogar ISOs do PC pelo cabo de rede.
   - Protecao dos nucleos: se o programa achar .ELF soltos da suite
     (RETROARCADE.ELF, CPS1.ELF, PCE.ELF...), pergunta se pode troca-los
     pelos .SYS protegidos. Se o .SYS ja existe, mostra os tamanhos e so
     troca se voce confirmar (o padrao e NAO).

 PASSO 7 - O LAUNCHER DO PS2
   No FreeMcBoot / PS2BBL, crie uma entrada apontando para o arquivo:
       RETROVOLT/FASTLOADER/FASTLOADER.ELF
   Ex. no pendrive: mass:/RETROVOLT/FASTLOADER/FASTLOADER.ELF
   Para o HD, use o caminho que o seu launcher usa para o HD exFAT.
   Ou abra pelo wLaunchELF/uLaunchELF navegando ate o arquivo.

 PASSO 8 - PRIMEIRA VEZ NO PS2
   1. Abra o FASTLOADER.ELF.
   2. Aparece o popup "PT-BR / ENG" (precisa de memory card no slot 1).
      Esquerda/direita escolhem, X grava. Nao pergunta mais.
   3. Pronto: tela principal com as abas.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 5. USANDO NO DIA A DIA
----------------------------------------------------------------------

 ABAS (L1 / R1 trocam):
   HD, USB, MX4SIO, MMCE   jogos de PS2 de cada aparelho
   PS1                     jogos de PS1 (pergunta HD ou USB)
   CDVD                    o disco que esta no leitor
   REDE (NETW em ingles)   jogos de PS2 do PC pelo cabo
   FILES                   gerenciador de arquivos

 IMPORTANTE: nenhuma aba le sozinha. Entre na aba e aperte X para
 carregar. SELECT le de novo (depois de copiar jogos novos).

 BOTOES NAS LISTAS:
   X               carrega a lista / inicia o jogo (pergunta antes)
   Triangulo       renomear (so o nome mostrado)
   Quadrado        modos de compatibilidade do Neutrino
   Circulo         sair para o menu do PS2
   Esquerda        adiciona aos favoritos (ate 10)
   L2 / R2         pagina anterior / proxima
   SELECT          atualizar a lista
   START           Extras
   START + SELECT  favoritos
   R3              troca MX4SIO <-> MMCE (so nas abas deles)

 EXTRAS (START):
   Desligar console / Reset / Creditos / Retro Arcade / Idioma

 INICIAR UM JOGO DE PS2:
   1. Escolha o jogo e aperte X.
   2. No popup, a linha MEMORY CARD: esquerda/direita escolhem
        FISICO (REAL)  = o cartao de verdade do slot 1
        VIRTUAL        = o arquivo .mcv daquele jogo
        CRIAR VIRTUAL  = cria o .mcv na hora e ja inicia
   3. X inicia.

 RETRO ARCADE:
   1. START > Extras > Retro Arcade.
   2. L1/R1 trocam o sistema (CPS1, CPS2, MVS, PC Engine, Neo Geo CD).
   3. X carrega a lista; X no jogo pergunta e inicia.
   4. Popup de iniciar: esquerda/direita escolhem 240p / 480i / 480p.
   5. Ao sair do jogo, volta sozinho ao Retro Arcade ("Voltando ao
      Retro Arcade"), no mesmo jogo.
   6. Voltar ao FastLoader: START no Retro Arcade > Voltar ao FastLoader.

 TROCAR O IDIOMA:
   START > Extras > Idioma. Vale para o FastLoader e o Retro Arcade.
   Para ver o popup da primeira vez de novo: apague
   mc0:RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\HDUI-LANG.CFG.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 6. MEMORY CARD VIRTUAL (MCV)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  - Um arquivo de 8 MB que o jogo enxerga como o memory card do slot 1.
  - Fica em RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\MEMORY CARD\ do MESMO aparelho do jogo.
  - Vale para HD, pendrive e MX4SIO. Nao vale para MMCE, rede, PS1 e
    disco no leitor.
  - Nome: o que vem antes do " - " no nome da ISO (ou os 30 primeiros
    caracteres). Ex.: "Phantom Brave - USA.iso" -> "Phantom Brave.mcv".
  - No pendrive, salvar demora (minutos). Nao desligue durante o save.
  - "MEMORY CARD: FISICO (NOME LONGO)": o caminho do jogo e comprido
    demais para o limite do console. Encurte o nome da ISO ou tire o
    jogo de subpastas.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 7. JOGAR PELA REDE (OPCIONAL)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. PS2 e PC no mesmo roteador (o PS2 por cabo). PS2 fat precisa do
     adaptador de rede.
  2. No PC: RetroVoltSuite.exe > aba Rede > escolha a pasta dos jogos >
     "Liberar no Firewall do Windows..." (so na 1a vez) > "Iniciar
     servidor".
  3. No PS2: aba REDE > X > acerte o IP do PS2 (os 3 primeiros numeros
     iguais aos do PC, o ultimo diferente) > X conecta.
  4. Nao feche o programa nem tire o cabo com o jogo rodando.
  5. Jogo da rede salva no memory card de verdade (sem MCV).


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 8. ATUALIZAR A SUITE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. Baixe o Vxx_retrovolt_full.zip mais novo.
  2. Descompacte na raiz do HD/pendrive, POR CIMA da pasta RETROVOLT.
  3. So isso. Jogos, capas, saves e memory cards virtuais ficam.
  Pode apagar, se ainda existirem:
    - a pasta antiga RETROVOLT\RETROARCADE\;
    - qualquer .ELF dentro de RETROVOLT\EXTRAS (CPS1.ELF, PCE.ELF,
      NEOGEOCD.ELF, RETROARCADE.ELF, _MVS.ELF...);
    - copias antigas do FastLoader (v2.0.8.ELF, v2.0.9.ELF...).
  NAO apague nem renomeie os .SYS de RETROVOLT\EXTRAS\A7F3C1.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 9. PROBLEMAS COMUNS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  Lista vazia
    -> Aperte X na aba (nenhuma aba le sozinha). "Nenhum ... detectado"
       = o aparelho nao respondeu (confira exFAT/FAT32). "Nenhuma ISO
       encontrada" = nao ha ISO nas pastas lidas.

  "NEUTRINO NAO ENCONTRADO"
    -> Falta a pasta do Neutrino em RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\ (pendrive, HD
       ou memory card). Copie neutrino.elf + config + modules.

  Jogo de PS2 trava / tela preta
    -> Teste os modos (Quadrado). Confira se o Neutrino esta completo e
       todo da mesma versao.

  "RETRO ARCADE NAO ENCONTRADO"
    -> Falta RETROVOLT\EXTRAS\A7F3C1\9B14.SYS. Copie o pacote de novo.

  "RETRO ARCADE DANIFICADO" ou nucleo "danificado"
    -> Um .SYS foi alterado ou copiado pela metade. Copie a pasta
       RETROVOLT\EXTRAS\A7F3C1 de novo, do pacote.

  Retro Arcade: "Pasta ... nao encontrada" ou lista vazia
    -> CPS1/CPS2/MVS: falta a pasta do sistema ou o rominfo dentro dela.
       PC Engine / Neo Geo CD: falta a pasta (PCE / NEOGEO-CD) ou o .SYS.

  CPS2: "Jogo sem cache"
    -> Gere o cache do jogo no PC e copie para EXTRAS\CPS2\CACHE.

  MVS: "Falta a BIOS"
    -> Coloque o neogeo.zip em EXTRAS\MVS\ROMS.

  PS1: "EMBER.ELF NAO ENCONTRADO"
    -> Falta EMBER\ember.elf na raiz do aparelho escolhido.

  MX4SIO ou MMCE nao aparece
    -> Os dois nao funcionam juntos. Na aba do outro, aperte R3.

  Sem capa
    -> A capa tem que estar em RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\CAPAS\PS2 (ou PS1)
       no MESMO aparelho do jogo. Use o RetroVoltSuite.exe.

  Qual versao eu tenho?
    -> START > Creditos: "Retro Volt Suite - FastLoader V2.1.1 - data".

  only when the multitap is switched on (it was forced again on every change and when the dialog opened, so the choice

commit.message:
PADEMU multitap: route each slot / port on its own, also for two-port polls

The SIO2 hook only handled single-port transfers when the multitap was emulated.
When the game polls port 1 and port 2 in one transfer, the old code ignored the
selected slot and, with the multitap on port 2, switched off the wrong command
(the real DS2 of port 1 stopped working).

- pademu_route.h: pure routing rules (real DS2 or emulated pad index) per port,
  tested on a PC by tools/test_pademu_route.c (555 checks, same result as before
  for every setup without the multitap)
- slot A not emulated = the real DS2 of the port; slots B-D always wireless
- game without multitap support: the multitap port is a plain pad (slot A), the
  other port stays with the real DS2
- debug builds log the routing decisions (PADEMU_DEBUG, needs the stdio import)

+/*
+ * PADEMU routing: which controller answers a pad command sent to a SIO2 port.
+ *
+ * Pure logic with no SDK dependency, so it can be unit tested on a PC (tools/test_pademu_route.c).
+ *
+ * Terms:
+ *  - pad index: the number of the controller on the PADEMU side (Bluetooth or USB pad 0..3).
+ *    Without the multitap it is the PS2 port (0 = 1P, 1 = 2P). With the multitap it is the slot (0 = A ... 3 = D).
+ *  - "real": the transfer is left to the console's own SIO2 hardware, so the DS2 plugged in the port answers.
+ *
+ * Without the multitap, a port is emulated when its pad is enabled in the menu.
+ *
+ * With the multitap, PADEMU emulates the multitap of one port (mtap_port). The other port is never touched.
+ *  - The game has not asked for the multitap (mtap_inited == 0): the port behaves as a plain pad, that is slot A.
+ *  - The game uses the multitap: the slot it selected last decides.
+ *  - Slot A: emulated when enabled in the menu, otherwise the real DS2 plugged in the port.
+ *  - Slots B, C, D: always PADEMU. Without a physical multitap there is no real pad that could be there; a slot
+ *    without a connected wireless pad answers "no pad".
+ */
+
+#ifndef PADEMU_ROUTE_H
+#define PADEMU_ROUTE_H
+
+#define PADEMU_ROUTE_REAL (-1)
+
+typedef struct
+{
+    unsigned char enabled;      // bit n: pad index n is enabled in the menu
+    unsigned char mtap_enabled; // multitap emulation switched on in the menu
+    unsigned char mtap_port;    // PS2 port (0/1) of the emulated multitap
+    unsigned char mtap_inited;  // the game asked the multitap for its slot count
+    unsigned char mtap_slot;    // slot the game selected last
+} pademu_route_t;
+
+// pad index to emulate for a pad command sent to `port` (0 or 1), or PADEMU_ROUTE_REAL
+static inline int pademu_route_port(const pademu_route_t *r, int port)
+{
+    int slot;
+
+    if (port < 0 || port > 1)
+        return PADEMU_ROUTE_REAL;
+
+    if (!r->mtap_enabled)
+        return ((r->enabled >> port) & 1) ? port : PADEMU_ROUTE_REAL;
+
+    if (port != r->mtap_port)
+        return PADEMU_ROUTE_REAL;
+
+    slot = r->mtap_inited ? (r->mtap_slot & 3) : 0;
+
+    if (slot == 0)
+        return (r->enabled & 1) ? 0 : PADEMU_ROUTE_REAL;
+
+    return slot;
+}
+
+// true when a multitap command (0x21 device) sent to `port` belongs to the multitap PADEMU emulates.
+// Commands for any other port go to the console's SIO2 untouched, so a real multitap there keeps working.
+static inline int pademu_route_is_mtap_port(const pademu_route_t *r, int port)
+{
+    return r->mtap_enabled && port >= 0 && port <= 1 && port == r->mtap_port;
+}
+
+#endif

commit.message: Improve PS1 disc-swap instructions and readability
Improve PS1 disc-swap instructions and readability
Fix USB boot device discovery and defer MX4SIO initialization

MMCE: commit the built mmceman and its patches

The fork's .gitignore drops *.irx and *.patch, so the lab's tree had
modules/mmce/mmceman.irx and the three patches build.sh applies while
the commit did not: a clean clone stopped at 'No rule to make target
modules/mmce/mmceman.irx'. Added past the ignore; the binary is the
one the hardware runs (md5 c77ab80c).

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

MMCE: commit the built mmceman and its patches

The fork's .gitignore drops *.irx and *.patch, so the lab's tree had
modules/mmce/mmceman.irx and the three patches build.sh applies while
the commit did not: a clean clone stopped at 'No rule to make target
modules/mmce/mmceman.irx'. Added past the ignore; the binary is the
one the hardware runs (md5 c77ab80c).

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

RA: hash PS1 images for POPS (.VCD)

raHashVcd reads a VCD the way rc_hash_psx reads a PS1 disc: skip the
1 MiB POPS header, map 2048-byte offsets onto 2352-byte MODE2 sectors,
take BOOT from SYSTEM.CNF (PSX.EXE if there is none), size from the
PS-X EXE header plus 2048, MD5 of name and bytes. Directory names now
compare case-insensitively, as rcheevos does for both consoles.

Not called yet. Host test on Blade (USA): 3e64b72f..., RA game 14491.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

PS1: list POPS/*.VCD with the PS2 games and launch POPStarter

The BDM pages append every POPS/<name>.VCD at the device root, marked
"PS1", with the serial read out of the image's SYSTEM.CNF. Launching
one copies POPS/POPSTARTER.ELF to XX.<name>.ELF if it is missing and
loads it as mass:/POPS/XX.<name>.ELF: POPStarter parses its argv[0],
and the SDK loader sets argv[0] to the path it loads. First USB device
only for now. The RA check hashes the VCD and asks the PC as for PS2.

A new UI setting, "PS1 and PS2 order": mixed by name, PS2 first or
PS1 first. The sort now compares game names, not badged text.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

PS1: drop the PS1/PS2 order setting

The build with it hung in the menu on hardware, and two probes showed
the hang is not in the POPS/ scan. Removed: the setting, the group and
sort-key fields on menu items, the sort by them. The sort is stock again.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

RA: name the sector source instead of a sentinel fd and a flag

read_at() took a file descriptor, with -100 standing for the drive and
a global flag switching it to VCD sectors around each call. It now
takes a struct ra_src with the descriptor and its kind. The PS1 code
reads SYSTEM.CNF in one place for the list and for the hash.

Host test: Blade.VCD 3e64b72f... (RA 14491) and Dynasty Warriors 2
29e392c7... (RA 19047), both unchanged. cppcheck finds nothing in the
changed lines.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

PS1: achievements under POPStarter

A PS1 image in POPS/<name>.VCD on a block device is listed with the PS2
games, marked PS1, hashed the way rcheevos hashes a PS1 disc and
launched through POPStarter (krHACKen r13) as mass:/POPS/XX.<name>.ELF.
Nothing of OPL runs under POPS, so the watch list travels inside
POPS/MODULE_9.IRX: OPL writes a copy of rapops with the IP
configuration, the serial and the list in its config block, POPStarter
loads it on the IOP after its own reset. rapops brings up DEV9, SMAP,
the TCP/IP stack and raudp as under a PS2 game, then starts rapull,
which reads the PS1 RAM windows through sceSifGetOtherData at 60 Hz and
hands the snapshots to raudp. The first request waits 25 seconds: one
during POPS's boot leaves the screen black.

POPStarter reads the game's device with its own driver. OPL puts the
BDMAssault pair for the device on the memory card before the launch
(mc?:/POPSTARTER/, RA_BDMA.TXT names the variant): mx4sio, ata, ilink.
USB stays on the built-in FAT32 driver unless "PS1 USB drive is exFAT"
is on in Settings; OPL cannot tell the formats apart, and the usbexfat
pair stalls POPS on its first video from a FAT32 stick.

Confirmed on hardware: Blade from a FAT32 stick and from an exFAT
drive, 60 snapshots a second, achievements unlock. Not done: PS1 from
MMCE, an APA HDD or a share; a second device of the same kind. The
MX4SIO, iLink and exFAT HDD pairs follow RiptOPL and have not been
run here.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the RA snapshot going when Mode 6 turns the IGR off

RA_OnVblank ran only from the IGR's VBLANK_END handler, and Mode 6
skips Install_IGR, so a game set to Mode 6 sent no telemetry at all.
Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus needs that mode: it takes the
IGR's padOpen patch for tampering and hides collectibles (xerabora
issue #15).

Under Mode 6 syshook now installs a handler that calls RA_OnVblank and
nothing else: no IGR thread, no padOpen patch, no CreateThread/ExecPS2
hooks. A reset asked for over the network has nothing to carry it out
in that mode, so IGR_RequestReset drops it.

Built, not run on hardware.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Remove the cheat engine and fix watch list chunk parsing

OPL-RA no longer carries PS2RD, reads no CHT files and has no cheat
menu. A list chunk whose data started with a whitespace byte lost that
byte, and the console refused the whole list.

-/*******************************************************************************
- *
- * CodeHandler - Process all codes in the code list and handle the different
- * code types.
- *
- ******************************************************************************/
-.ent    CodeHandler
-CodeHandler:
-    /*
-     * $t0 - ptr to code list
-     * $t1 - ptr to jump table for code types
-     * $t3 - total number of codes
-     * $t4 - number of codes done
-     */
-    lw      $t3, numcodes
-    beqz    $t3, ch_ret
-    li      $t4, 0
-    la      $t0, codelist
-    la      $t1, type_tab
-ch_loop:
-    /*
-     * $t2 - ptr to current code
-     * $a0 - RAM address
-     * $a1 - code value
-     */
-    sll     $at, $t4, 3
-    addu    $t2, $t0, $at
-    lw      $a0, 0($t2)
-    beqz    $a0, next
-    srl     $a2, $a0, 28
-    sll     $a2, 2
-    addu    $a2, $t1
-    lw      $t5, 0($a2)
-    beqz    $t5, next
-    sll     $a0, 7
-    srl     $a0, 7
-
-    /* jump to code type handler */
-    jr      $t5
-    lw      $a1, 4($t2)
-type_0:
-    /*
-     * "8-bit constant write"
-     *
-     * 0-aaaaaaa 000000vv
-     *
-     * Constantly writes the 8-bit value @v to address @a.
-     */
-    b       next
-    sb      $a1, 0($a0)
-type_1:
-    /*
-     * "16-bit constant write"
-     *
-     * 1-aaaaaaa 0000vvvv
-     *
-     * Constantly writes the 16-bit value @v to address @a.
-     */
-    b       next
-    sh      $a1, 0($a0)
-type_2:
-    /*
-     * "32-bit constant write"
-     *
-     * 2-aaaaaaa vvvvvvvv
-     *
-     * Constantly writes the 32-bit value @v to address @a.
-     */
-    b       next
-    sw      $a1, 0($a0)
-type_3:
-    /*
-     * "Increment / Decrement"
-     *
-     * 8-bit increment
-     * 3-00000vv 0aaaaaaa
-     *
-     * 8-bit decrement
-     * 3-01000vv 0aaaaaaa
-     *
-     * 16-bit increment
-     * 3-020vvvv 0aaaaaaa
-     *
-     * 16-bit decrement
-     * 3-030vvvv 0aaaaaaa
-     *
-     * 32-bit increment
-     * 3-0400000 0aaaaaaa
-     * vvvvvvvv 00000000
-     *
-     * 32-bit decrement
-     * 3-0500000 0aaaaaaa
-     * vvvvvvvv 00000000
-     *
-     * It increments/decrements the current value at address @a by value @v.
-     */
-    srl     $t6, $a0, 20
-    andi    $at, $t6, 1     # 0=inc, 1=dec
-    andi    $a0, 0xffff
-    sll     $a1, 7
-    srl     $a1, 7
-    andi    $t6, 6          # zero for 8 bit
-    andi    $a2, $t6, 2     # non-zero for 16 bit
-    beqzl   $t6, 1f
-    lbu     $t5, 0($a1)
-    bnezl   $a2, 1f
-    lhu     $t5, 0($a1)
-    lw      $t5, 0($a1)
-    lw      $a0, 8($t2)
-    addiu   $t4, 1
-1:
-    beqzl   $at, 2f
-    addu    $t5, $a0
-    subu    $t5, $a0
-2:
-    beqzl   $t6, next
-    sb      $t5, 0($a1)
-    bnezl   $a2, next
-    sh      $t5, 0($a1)
-    b       next
-    sw      $t5, 0($a1)
-type_4:
-    /*
-     * "32-bit constant serial write"
-     *
-     * 4-aaaaaaa nnnnssss
-     * vvvvvvvv iiiiiiii
-     *
-     * Starting with address @a, this code type will write the 32-bit value
-     * @v to @n addresses. In each cycle, the address is incremented by
-     * @s * 4 and the value is incremented by @i.
-     */
-    lw      $a2, 8($t2)
-    lw      $a3, 12($t2)
-    srl     $t5, $a1, 16
-    andi    $a1, 0xffff
-    sll     $a1, 2
-1:
-    nop
-    nop
-    sw      $a2, 0($a0)
-    addu    $a2, $a3
-    addiu   $t5, -1
-    bgtz    $t5, 1b
-    addu    $a0, $a1
-    b       next
-    addiu   $t4, 1
-type_5:
-    /*
-     * "Copy bytes"
-     *
-     * 5-sssssss nnnnnnnn
-     * 0ddddddd 00000000
-     *
-     * Copies a block of @n bytes from source address @s to destination
-     * address @d.
-     */
-    lw      $a2, 8($t2)
-1:
-    lb      $t5, 0($a0)
-    nop
-    sb      $t5, 0($a2)
-    addiu   $a2, 1
-    addiu   $a1, -1
-    bgtz    $a1, 1b
-    addiu   $a0, 1
-    b       next
-    addiu   $t4, 1
-type_6:
-    /*
-     * "Pointer write"
-     *
-     * 8-bit write
-     * 6-aaaaaaa 000000vv
-     * 00000000 iiiiiiii
-     *
-     * 16-bit write
-     * 6-aaaaaaa 0000vvvv
-     * 00010000 iiiiiiii
-     *
-     * 32-bit write
-     * 6-aaaaaaa vvvvvvvv
-     * 00020000 iiiiiiii
-     *
-     * Loads 32-bit base address from address @a, adds offset @i to it, and
-     * constantly writes the value @v to the final address.
-     */
-    lw      $t5, 0($a0)
-    li      $at, 0x3ffffffc
-    and     $t5, $at
-    beqz    $t5, 1f
-    lhu     $a2, 10($t2)
-    lw      $a3, 12($t2)
-    addu    $t5, $a3
-    beqzl   $a2, 1f
-    sb      $a1, 0($t5)
-    addiu   $a2, -1
-    beqzl   $a2, 1f
-    sh      $a1, 0($t5)
-    sw      $a1, 0($t5)
-1:
-    b       next
-    addiu   $t4, 1
-type_7:
-    /*
-     * "Boolean operation"
-     *
-     * 8-bit OR
-     * 7-aaaaaaa 000000vv
-     *
-     * 16-bit OR
-     * 7-aaaaaaa 0010vvvv
-     *
-     * 8-bit AND
-     * 7-aaaaaaa 002000vv
-     *
-     * 16-bit AND
-     * 7-aaaaaaa 0030vvvv
-     *
-     * 8-bit XOR
-     * 7-aaaaaaa 004000vv
-     *
-     * 16-bit XOR
-     * 7-aaaaaaa 0050vvvv
-     *
-     * Performs a bitwise logical operation between value @v and the value
-     * stored at address @a.
-     */
-    srl     $t6, $a1, 20
-    andi    $at, $t6, 1     # 0=8 bit, 1=16 bit
-    andi    $t6, 6          # 0=OR, 2=AND, 4=XOR
-    bnezl   $at, 1f
-    lhu     $t5, 0($a0)
-    lbu     $t5, 0($a0)
-1:
-    beqzl   $t6, 2f
-    or      $t5, $a1
-    addiu   $t6, -2
-    beqzl   $t6, 2f
-    and     $t5, $a1
-    xor     $t5, $a1
-2:
-    bnezl   $at, next
-    sh      $t5, 0($a0)
-    b       next
-    sb      $t5, 0($a0)
-type_c:
-    /*
-     * "32-bit do all following codes if equal to"
-     *
-     * C-aaaaaaa vvvvvvvv
-     *
-     * All following codes will be executed only if 32-bit value at address
-     * @a is equal to value @v.
-     */
-    lw      $t5, 0($a0)
-    bne     $t5, $a1, ch_ret
-    nop
-    b       next
-    nop
-type_d:
-    /*
-     * "Do multi-lines if conditional"
-     *
-     * 16-bit test
-     * D-aaaaaaa nnt0vvvv
-     *
-     * 8-bit test
-     * D-aaaaaaa nnt100vv
-     *
-     * Compares value at address @a to value @v, and executes next @n code
-     * lines only if the test condition @t is true. Values for @t are:
-     *   0 equal      1 not equal
-     *   2 less than  3 greater than
-     *   4 NAND       5 AND
-     *   6 NOR        7 OR
-     */
-    srl     $a3, $a1, 16
-    andi    $a3, 1
-    srl     $t6, $a1, 20
-    srl     $a2, $a1, 24
-    beqzl   $a2, 1f          # set @n to 1 if 0 for compatibility
-    li      $a2, 1
-1:
-    beqz    $a3, 2f
-    andi    $t6, 7
-    lbu     $t5, 0($a0)
-    b       3f
-    andi    $a1, 0xff
-2:
-    lhu     $t5, 0($a0)
-    andi    $a1, 0xffff
-3:
-    beqzl   $t6, 4f         # equal
-    subu    $t5, $a1
-    li      $at, 1          # not equal
-    beql    $t6, $at, 5f
-    subu    $t5, $a1
-    li      $at, 2          # less than
-    beql    $t6, $at, 5f
-    sltu    $t5, $a1
-    li      $at, 3          # greater than
-    beql    $t6, $at, 5f
-    sltu    $t5, $a1, $t5
-    li      $at, 4          # NAND
-    beql    $t6, $at, 4f
-    and     $t5, $a1
-    li      $at, 5          # AND
-    beql    $t6, $at, 5f
-    and     $t5, $a1
-    li      $at, 6          # NOR
-    beql    $t6, $at, 4f
-    or      $t5, $a1
-    b       5f              # OR
-    or      $t5, $a1
-4:                          # skip if non-zero
-    bnezl   $t5, next
-    addu    $t4, $a2
-    b       next
-    nop
-5:                          # skip if zero
-    beqzl   $t5, next
-    addu    $t4, $a2
-    b       next
-    nop
-type_e:
-    /*
-     * "Do multi-lines if conditional (deprecated)"
-     *
-     * 16-bit test
-     * E-0nnvvvv taaaaaaa
-     *
-     * 8-bit test
-     * E-1nn00vv taaaaaaa
-     *
-     * This type is internally converted to the D type - see above.
-     */
-    andi    $a2, $a0, 0xffff
-    srl     $at, $a1, 28
-    sll     $at, 20
-    or      $a2, $at
-    srl     $at, $a0, 24
-    sll     $at, 16
-    or      $a2, $at
-    srl     $at, $a0, 16
-    sll     $at, 24
-    or      $a2, $at
-    sll     $a0, $a1, 7
-    srl     $a0, 7
-    li      $t5, 0xd0000000
-    or      $t5, $a0
-    move    $a1, $a2
-    sw      $t5, 0($t2)     # store converted address
-    b       type_d
-    sw      $a1, 4($t2)     # store converted value
-next:
-    /* next code */
-    addiu   $t4, 1
-    sltu    $at, $t4, $t3
-    bnez    $at, ch_loop
-    nop
-ch_ret:
-    jr      $ra
-    nop

-/*******************************************************************************
- *
- * HookSetupThread - Pre-call hook function for syscall SetupThread().
- *
- * It runs through all hooks in the hook list and hard-codes a jal to
- * EngineHandler() if a hook's value is equal to the opcode at the hook address;
- * replaced opcodes are backed up. After processing the boot codes, it calls
- * the original SetupThread() function.
- *
- * NOTE: Only the _first_ matching hook will be activated.
- *
- * Here are the syscall parameters - those regs must not be modified!
- *
- * void *SetupThread(void *gp, $a0
- *    void *stack,             $a1
- *    s32 stack_size,          $a2
- *    void *args,              $a3
- *    void *root_func)         $t0
- *
- ******************************************************************************/
-.ent    HookSetupThread
-HookSetupThread:
-    addiu   $sp, -0x10
-    sd      $ra, 0($sp)
-
-    /*
-     * $t1 - number of hooks to do
-     * $t3 - ptr to hook list entry
-     * $v0 - hook address
-     */
-    lw      $t1, numhooks
-    beqz    $t1, 3f
-    nop
-    la      $t3, hooklist
-1:
-    /* hook only if opcodes are equal */
-    lw      $v0, 0($t3)
-    beqz    $v0, 2f
-    lw      $v1, 4($t3)
-    lw      $t2, 0($v0)
-    bne     $t2, $v1, 2f
-    nop
-
-    /* back up opcodes */
-    la      $at, eh_backup
-    sw      $t2, 0($at)
-    lw      $v1, 4($v0)
-    sw      $v1, 4($at)
-
-    /* inject jal to engine handler */
-    lw      $v1, jal_EngineHandler
-    sw      $v1, 0($v0)
-    b       3f
-    sw      $zero, 4($v0)
-2:
-    /* next hook */
-    addiu   $t1, -1
-    bgtz    $t1, 1b
-    addiu   $t3, 8
-3:
-    ld      $ra, 0($sp)
-    addiu   $sp, 0x10
-
-    /* jump to original SetupThread() */
-    lw      $t1, Old_SetupThread    # $t1 -> original SetupThread function
-    j       $t1
-    nop
-.end    HookSetupThread

+/*
+  RA: what OPL writes into its copy of rapops (modules/network/rapops)
+  before a PS1 launch. POPStarter loads that copy as MODULE_#.IRX
+  without arguments, so the module carries its configuration: OPL
+  finds the block by the magic and fills it in.
+*/
+#ifndef __RAPOPS_CFG_H__
+#define __RAPOPS_CFG_H__
+
+#include "ra_watch.h"
+
+#define RAPOPS_MAGIC     "RAPOPS01"
+#define RAPOPS_IPCFG_MAX 64
+
+struct rapops_cfg
+{
+    char magic[8] __attribute__((nonstring)); /* RAPOPS_MAGIC */
+    int ipcfg_len;                            /* 0: not configured, the module stays out */
+    char ipcfg[RAPOPS_IPCFG_MAX];             /* "ip\0mask\0gateway\0", as SMAP takes it */
+    char game_id[16];                         /* the serial, e.g. "SLUS_012.15" */
+    /* the watch list for rapull, the reader on the IOP; count 0: no list */
+    unsigned int count;
+    unsigned int bytes;
+    unsigned int node_count;
+    unsigned int list[RA_WATCH_MAX];
+    struct ra_node nodes[RA_NODE_MAX];
+};
+
+#endif
